first.rationale: Competitor pricing pressure makes promotional_pricing tempting, but memory_73 explicitly warns it harms 30-day retention and should not be generalized as a strategy—pursuing it risks trading long-term qualified revenue for short-term acquisition, conflicting with the primary objective. Meanwhile, onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ, and memory_31 (signup simplification) plus memory_86 (shortened onboarding) both show durable, low-risk lifts in activation/time-to-value for self-serve SMB accounts—directly addressing the observed internal declines without known downstream harm. I verify memory_73 to confirm the retention risk is real before ruling promotional_pricing out, and memory_31 to confirm the onboarding simplification result is robust before committing this week's single experiment slot to it. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives are valuable but don't address the acute, measurable degradations happening right now, and activation_messaging is a plausible alternative but has less direct evidence tied to the onboarding completion metric specifically declining.
